levels.name: Fundamentals
levels.what: The foundation: taught in the first weeks on a floor or the first term of a program, needed before working unsupervised, and shared by many careers.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.what: The working trade: what a qualified operator, technician or inspector does alone and is paid for.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.what: Where a trade crystallizes into a specialization: work that takes a further credential, years of practice or engineering judgment.

domains.name: Materials
domains.what: Changing what a material is or how its surface looks and behaves: heat treatment, surface treatment, peening and thermal spray, paint and wood finishing, composites, printing, making, dyeing and finishing yarn and fabric, and materials testing and engineering.

groups.name: Heat treatment
groups.what: Changing a metal's hardness and structure in a furnace: relieving stress, annealing, hardening, case hardening, vacuum and pressure cycles.

groups.name: Age hardening
groups.what: Bringing aluminum, titanium and nickel alloys to temper by solution treatment, quench and aging.

groups.name: Furnace pyrometry
groups.what: Proving that a furnace or autoclave measures and holds the temperature it claims.

groups.name: Materials testing
groups.what: Testing what a material is and has become: its alloy, hardness, strength and structure under the microscope.

groups.name: Materials engineering
groups.what: Choosing, specifying and qualifying the materials and processes a product is made from.

groups.name: Surface treatment
groups.what: Treating metal in chemical and electrolytic baths: conversion coating, passivation, anodizing, electropolishing and plating.

groups.name: Peening and thermal spray
groups.what: Changing a surface by impact or by sprayed coating: shot peening for fatigue life, thermal spray for wear and heat.

groups.name: Paint pretreatment
groups.what: Getting a surface ready to hold paint: stripping and blasting, phosphate conversion and electrocoat primer.

groups.name: Paint application
groups.what: Putting paint, powder and sealer on: masking, sealing seams, spraying by gun and by robot, powder coating, matching color and repairing defects.

groups.name: Coating inspection
groups.what: Checking a coating once it is on: thickness, defects, appearance and adhesion.

groups.name: Wood finishing
groups.what: Finishing wood: sanding, staining and glazing, flatline coating, and touch-up and repair.

groups.name: Printing
groups.what: Putting ink on paper, board, labels and film on offset, flexographic, digital and screen presses, and holding its color by measurement.

groups.name: Prepress
groups.what: Preparing every print job: checking and imposing the files, making the plates and proofs, and keeping prepress, proof and press on one color standard.

groups.name: Composite fabrication
groups.what: Building a laminate: cutting and kitting plies, preparing the tool, laying up by hand and by machine, winding, infusing, and trimming the cured part.

groups.name: Open molding
groups.what: Making fiberglass parts in an open mold: spraying the gelcoat and laminating it by chopper gun.

groups.name: Composite curing
groups.what: Bagging a layup and curing it in an autoclave or oven, from thermocouple placement to writing and controlling the cycle.

groups.name: Composite bonding
groups.what: Joining composite and metal details with adhesive: surface preparation, film and paste adhesives, secondary bonds and co-cure.

groups.name: Composite repair
groups.what: Assessing damage in composite structure and restoring it by bonded or bolted repair.

groups.name: Yarn making
groups.what: Turning fiber into yarn: opening and carding, spinning, winding and twisting, and piecing up ends.

groups.name: Fabric forming
groups.what: Turning yarn or fiber into fabric: warp preparation, weaving, knitting, tufting, braiding and nonwoven lines.

groups.name: Dyeing and finishing
groups.what: Giving a textile its color and its final width, hand and performance: dyeing, finishing, and working out the dye recipe.

domains.name: Engineering
domains.what: Designing parts, circuits and systems and the processes that make them: drawings and design data, CAD, design methods, electrical design, manufacturing engineering and systems engineering.

groups.name: CAD and drawings
groups.what: The model, the drawing and the controlled data a shop builds from: drafting in two dimensions, modeling in three, assemblies and released revisions.

groups.name: Pattern design
groups.what: Drafting, grading and marking the patterns sewn products are cut from, and correcting them from fittings.

groups.name: Design methods
groups.what: The analysis behind a design: manufacturability, tolerance stacks, failure modes, additive design, finite element analysis and the fixtures and tools a part is made on.

groups.name: Engineering analysis
groups.what: Working out by calculation and simulation whether a design will hold, cool, float and flow as it must.

groups.name: Electrical design
groups.what: Designing circuits and the electrical side of machines: schematics, board layout and controls drawings.

groups.name: Manufacturing engineering
groups.what: Designing how the work is done: instructions, time standards, balanced lines, error-proof stations and the data that shows what is happening.

groups.name: Truss design
groups.what: Laying out, designing and repairing roof and floor trusses in truss design software.

groups.name: Systems engineering
groups.what: Stating what a system must do and planning how it will be proven.

domains.name: Production
domains.what: What everyone on a floor shares: reading the print and the instruction, keeping lots traceable, working in controlled rooms, moving material and improving the work.

groups.name: Shop basics
groups.what: Reading what the job calls for: the drawing, the written instruction and the arithmetic between them.

groups.name: Lot control
groups.what: Keeping every lot tied to its recipe, materials and history as it moves through the plant, from the mark on the part to the record in the system.

groups.name: Controlled environments
groups.what: Working in rooms where particles and static are the enemy: gowning, cleanroom conduct and electrostatic discharge control.

groups.name: Foreign object control
groups.what: Keeping loose hardware, debris and tools out of flight hardware.

groups.name: Material handling
groups.what: Lifting and moving loads, and people, with trucks, cranes, rigging and lifts.

groups.name: Continuous improvement
groups.what: The lean and Six Sigma methods a plant uses to organize an area, standardize the work, measure its losses and remove them.

domains.name: Machining
domains.what: Cutting metal and wood to size: manual and CNC machines, grinding, EDM, setup and programming, sawmilling and saw filing, and woodworking machines.

groups.name: Manual machining
groups.what: Making a part by hand: benchwork, drilling and tapping, and the engine lathe and knee mill a machinist learns first.

groups.name: CNC setup
groups.what: Getting a CNC machine ready to cut and keeping it on size: the control, offsets, workholding, tools measured off the machine, probing, speeds and feeds.

groups.name: CNC machining
groups.what: Running machining centers and lathes, from three-axis milling and turning to multi-axis, Swiss-type and large aerospace and casting work.

groups.name: Grinding
groups.what: Finishing hardened parts to size and surface with abrasives: precision grinding, wheel dressing, honing, lapping and jig grinding.

groups.name: Sawmilling
groups.what: Breaking logs down into lumber: primary breakdown, edging and trimming, and sorting and stacking.

groups.name: Saw filing
groups.what: The filing room's trade: grinding, swaging, tipping and benching band and circular saws.

groups.name: Electrical discharge machining
groups.what: Cutting hardened metal with a spark, by wire or by shaped electrode.

groups.name: CNC programming
groups.what: Writing the program a CNC machine runs: G-code by hand, toolpaths in CAM software, and proving them in simulation.

groups.name: Woodworking machines
groups.what: The machines of cabinet, furniture, sign and millwork plants: stationary machines, panel saws, CNC routers, edgebanders, moulders and wide-belt sanders.

domains.name: Fabrication
domains.what: Shaping and joining metal, plastic, rubber and glass: welding, brazing, cutting, sheet metal, shipfitting, stamping and dies, casting, molding, the mill processes (melting, rolling, forging and drawing), paperboard and print finishing, the bench trades of dental and optical laboratories, jewelry and signs, and additive manufacturing.

groups.name: Arc welding
groups.what: Reading the weld symbol, fitting the joint and welding it by MIG, stick, flux-cored and TIG, by hand and by robot, up to pipe and orbital work.

groups.name: Alloy welding
groups.what: Welding the metals that punish mistakes: stainless steel, aluminum, titanium and aluminum-lithium.

groups.name: Resistance welding
groups.what: Spot welding sheet by hand gun, pedestal or robot, and keeping the electrodes in condition.

groups.name: Beam and friction welding
groups.what: Machine welding without an arc: laser welding and brazing, friction stir and electron beam.

groups.name: Brazing methods
groups.what: Joining with a filler that melts below the base metal, by torch and in the furnace.

groups.name: Weld quality
groups.what: Proving a weld and the people and procedures behind it: visual inspection, destructive tests and qualification to a code.

groups.name: Cutting processes
groups.what: Cutting plate and sheet to shape by flame, plasma, laser and waterjet.

groups.name: Sheet metal work
groups.what: Laying out, bending and forming sheet and plate into finished shapes.

groups.name: Heavy fabrication
groups.what: Fitting and welding plate, beams and shells into structures, tanks and pressure vessels.

groups.name: Shipfitting
groups.what: Fitting pipe and structure in a ship or plant.

groups.name: Stamping and dies
groups.what: Running presses and the dies in them, from operating and setting a die to fitting, spotting and trying one out.

groups.name: Forging
groups.what: Shaping metal under hammers, presses and headers: open-die and impression-die forging, setting the dies, cold heading, thread rolling and ring rolling.

groups.name: Rolling and extrusion
groups.what: Shaping metal in a mill: hot and cold rolling and setting the stands, roll forming and welded tube, and extruding aluminum.

groups.name: Wire and cable
groups.what: Making wire and cable: drawing rod down to wire, and stranding and cabling it into conductors and cables.

groups.name: Melt shop
groups.what: Melting, refining and casting metal in a steel mill or foundry melt shop: arc and induction furnaces, ladle refining and iron treatment, sampling, linings, and continuous and direct-chill casting.

groups.name: Die casting
groups.what: Casting aluminum under pressure: the melt, the machine and its die, the spray, the shot and the trim.

skills.name: Die Casting Die Setup and Maintenance

groups.name: Foundry casting
groups.what: Casting in sand and in ceramic shells: molds, cores, wax patterns, pouring and knockout.

groups.name: Plastics molding
groups.what: Making plastic parts: injection molding from the press to the process, extrusion and blow molding.

groups.name: Rubber processing
groups.what: Mixing, forming and vulcanizing rubber, and building tires.

groups.name: Glass forming and fabrication
groups.what: Forming hot glass into containers, and cutting, edging, tempering, laminating and building insulating units from flat glass, with the inspection both need.

groups.name: Additive manufacturing
groups.what: Printing parts in metal and polymer: handling the powder, preparing and running the build and finishing what comes out.

groups.name: Corrugating and converting
groups.what: Combining corrugated board, and cutting, folding, gluing, slitting and rewinding paper and board into products.

groups.name: Print finishing
groups.what: The bindery: cutting, folding, stitching, binding and foil stamping printed sheets.

groups.name: Sign making
groups.what: What a sign plant does that no other plant does: channel letters, large-format prints, vinyl graphics and the wiring of an electric sign.

groups.name: Dental laboratory
groups.what: Making crowns, bridges and dentures to a prescription: models and dies, dental CAD, milling and sintering, ceramics and dentures.

groups.name: Ophthalmic lenses
groups.what: Making prescription spectacle lenses: surfacing, coating, edging and mounting, and verifying the power.

groups.name: Jewelry making
groups.what: The bench work of jewelry: fabrication and repair in precious metal, and setting stones.

domains.name: Assembly
domains.what: Putting products together: fastening, fits and alignment, the assembly of machines, medical devices, vehicles, RVs, aircraft, rocket engines and spacecraft, cabinets, furniture and trusses, sewn goods and footwear, and building up and maintaining munitions, weapons and survival equipment.

groups.name: Assembly practice
groups.what: What every assembler does at a station: hand and torque tools, securing fasteners, checking the build and reworking it.

groups.name: Precision mechanical assembly
groups.what: Fitting bearings and interference fits, balancing what rotates and building engines and gear trains.

groups.name: Medical device assembly
groups.what: The assembly processes of medical devices: work under the microscope, light-cure bonding and the thermal forming of catheters.

groups.name: Fluid system assembly
groups.what: Building the tubes and fittings that carry fluid and proving them: fitting make-up, tube bending, precision cleaning, and proof and leak tests.

groups.name: Machine tool building
groups.what: Building a machine tool and making it accurate: guides, ballscrews and spindles, scraping and alignment, then measuring and compensating its errors.

groups.name: Structural fastening
groups.what: Fastening aircraft structure: knowing the fastener, preparing the hole and installing rivets, pins, lockbolts and nutplates.

groups.name: Cabinet and furniture making
groups.what: Building cabinets, furniture and millwork: hand-tool work, joinery, casework, hardware, veneering and curved work.

groups.name: Truss and wall panel assembly
groups.what: Sawing, jigging, plating and pressing trusses and framing wall panels in a component plant.

groups.name: Airframe assembly
groups.what: Building an airframe: sealing and shimming joints, installing skins, lines and control surfaces, joining major sections and rigging the controls.

groups.name: Vehicle body assembly
groups.what: Building a vehicle body from stamped panels: mechanical joining, structural adhesive, hemming, framing, fitting closures and finishing the metal.

groups.name: Vehicle final assembly
groups.what: The stations of a vehicle's final line, from routing the harness to marrying the powertrain and filling the fluids.

groups.name: RV and modular building
groups.what: Building the living space of an RV or a factory-built home on a line: laminated walls and roof, roofing, plumbing, propane, and the cabinets and interior.

groups.name: Rocket engine build
groups.what: Making and assembling a liquid rocket engine: injectors and cooling channels, valves and turbopumps, the engine itself and its refurbishment.

groups.name: Launch vehicle integration
groups.what: Installing the tanks, pressure vessels, steering and separation hardware of a launch vehicle, and mating the sections of a missile.

groups.name: Spacecraft integration
groups.what: Building a satellite or spacecraft: structure and units, insulation, thrusters, fluid loops and the mechanisms that deploy.

groups.name: Recovery and reuse
groups.what: The hardware that brings a vehicle back and the inspection that lets it fly again: heat shield tiles, parachutes and post-flight inspection.

groups.name: Survival equipment
groups.what: Sewing, inspecting and servicing the gear that keeps aircrew alive.

groups.name: Cut and sew
groups.what: Making sewn products from roll goods: reading the tech pack, spreading, cutting, sewing and constructing the product.

groups.name: Upholstery
groups.what: Springing, padding, covering and tufting upholstered furniture.

groups.name: Footwear and leather goods
groups.what: Cutting leather and building shoes and boots on the last.

groups.name: Weapons and munitions
groups.what: Building up, inspecting and maintaining guns, missiles, torpedoes and ammunition.

domains.name: Electronics
domains.what: Building electronics and wiring, and keeping fielded systems working: soldering and board assembly, rework, harnesses and cabling, power electronics, servers and devices, and the upkeep of radar, radio and navigation equipment.

groups.name: Soldering and rework
groups.what: Soldering by hand to the IPC standards, judging the joint, finding the failed part and replacing it.

groups.name: Board assembly line
groups.what: Running and programming the machines that build a circuit board: paste printing, placement, reflow, wave soldering and automatic inspection.

groups.name: Circuit board fabrication
groups.what: Making bare printed circuit boards: imaging the layers, pressing multilayers, drilling and routing the panels, and testing every net.

groups.name: Coating and potting
groups.what: Protecting a finished circuit with conformal coating or resin.

groups.name: Cable and harness assembly
groups.what: Building wiring: crimping and terminating wire, assembling connectors and harnesses, securing bundles, bonding and grounding, coaxial and fiber cables.

groups.name: Electromechanical assembly
groups.what: Building boards, wiring and devices into a finished enclosure: the box build and the industrial control panel.

groups.name: Electronics cooling
groups.what: Getting heat out of electronics: thermal interface materials, heat sinks, cold plates and coolant loops.

skills.name: Cold Plate and Coolant Loop Assembly

groups.name: Power electronics
groups.what: Building inverters, converters and the power semiconductor modules inside them.

groups.name: Transformer build
groups.what: Building power and distribution transformers: winding the coils, stacking the core, assembling core and coil, drying and filling the tank, and the routine tests.

groups.name: Server integration
groups.what: Building servers and racks: installing components, mounting and cabling the rack, then configuring firmware, storage and the operating system.

groups.name: Consumer device assembly
groups.what: Assembling phones, laptops and similar devices: battery, display, camera, seals and sensor calibration.

groups.name: Communication terminals
groups.what: Building the radio and laser terminals that carry data to and between satellites.

groups.name: Optics
groups.what: Building and proving optics: handling and cleaning them, polishing them, aligning them, cementing and bonding them, and testing them by interferometer.

groups.name: Fielded electronic systems
groups.what: Keeping radar, sonar, radio, navigation and weapon electronics working after they leave the factory.

domains.name: Automation
domains.what: Making machines run themselves: instrumentation, PLCs, motion and drives, industrial networks, robots and machine vision.

groups.name: Instrumentation
groups.what: The sensors, transmitters and loops a control system reads and holds: finding them on the diagram, wiring, calibrating and tuning them.

groups.name: PLC programming
groups.what: Programming and troubleshooting the controllers that run a machine, and the operator screens that go with them.

groups.name: Motion and drives
groups.what: Setting up the drives that turn motors and axes, and tuning servo loops.

groups.name: Networks and SCADA
groups.what: The networks that tie controllers, drives and plant software together, and the system that gathers and shows their data.

groups.name: Industrial robots
groups.what: Running, programming and maintaining industrial robots: the teach pendant, end-of-arm tooling, programs, mastering and offline simulation.

groups.name: Cell design and machine safety
groups.what: Designing a robot cell and the controls that protect people: tooling, layout, safeguarding and safety circuits.

groups.name: Machine vision
groups.what: Making a camera system see a part reliably and programming it to find, measure and inspect.

domains.name: Semiconductor
domains.what: Making chips: lithography, deposition, etch, diffusion and implant, wafer metrology and defects, packaging, test and failure analysis.

groups.name: Contamination control
groups.what: Handling wafers without damaging or contaminating them, and counting the particles a room, a liquid or a tool adds.

groups.name: Lithography
groups.what: Printing the circuit pattern: resist coat, exposure and develop, immersion and EUV scanners, process windows and mask correction.

groups.name: Thin film deposition
groups.what: Putting films on a wafer from gases and sputter targets: CVD, PVD, epitaxy and atomic layer deposition.

groups.name: Plasma etch
groups.what: Transferring the pattern into the film with a reactive plasma and stopping at the right layer.

groups.name: Wet processing
groups.what: Cleaning, etching, stripping and polishing wafers with liquid chemistry and slurry.

groups.name: Diffusion and implant
groups.what: Growing oxide, annealing and doping wafers in furnaces, lamp tools and implanters.

groups.name: Wafer metrology
groups.what: Measuring what the process made on the wafer: line width, overlay, film thickness, sheet resistance and stress.

groups.name: Defect and yield
groups.what: Finding defects on wafers, naming them and tracing them, with tool sensor data, back to the step that caused them.

groups.name: Chip packaging
groups.what: Turning a finished wafer into packaged devices: dicing, die attach, wire and flip chip bonding, underfill and molding.

groups.name: Probe and final test
groups.what: Testing every die on the wafer and every packaged device electrically.

groups.name: Failure analysis
groups.what: Finding the physical cause of a failed chip: fault isolation, cross-sections, electron microscopy samples and depth profiles.

domains.name: Battery and electric drive
domains.what: Making battery cells, modules and packs, and the electric motors and drive units they power.

groups.name: Electrode manufacturing
groups.what: Making the electrode: mixing slurry, coating and drying it on foil, calendering and slitting.

groups.name: Cell assembly
groups.what: Building the cell in the dry room: notching and stacking or winding, tab welding, insertion, electrolyte fill and sealing.

groups.name: Cell finishing
groups.what: Bringing a sealed cell to life and sorting it: formation, degassing, aging, voltage checks and grading.

groups.name: Module and pack assembly
groups.what: Building cells into modules and packs: interconnects and busbars, cooling, high-voltage wiring, management electronics and sealing.

groups.name: Electric motor build
groups.what: Building a traction motor: winding or hairpin stators, impregnation, rotor magnets, housing and final assembly.

groups.name: Pack and motor testing
groups.what: Proving a finished pack or drive unit at the end of the line: leak tests and the electrical and performance tests.

domains.name: Process
domains.what: Food, beverage, pharmaceutical and chemical processing: meat, baking, dairy, milling, brewing, winemaking and distilling, biologics, batching, filling, sterilization, aseptic work and laboratory analysis under GMP, running a chemical plant or a refinery, pulp and paper, wood panels and kilns, handling fuels, and operating a nuclear plant.

groups.name: GMP and sanitation
groups.what: Working the way a regulated plant must: good manufacturing practice, food safety controls, cleaning and sanitizing, and proving a process by validation.

groups.name: Food processing
groups.what: Making food and beverage product: batching and blending, carbonating and drying.

groups.name: Meat and poultry processing
groups.what: Turning animals into meat: humane handling and stunning, dressing the carcass, the antimicrobial step, breaking it into cuts, boning and trimming, keeping the knife, and cooking and smoking processed meat.

groups.name: Baking
groups.what: Making bread, buns, cakes and crackers at production scale: mixing dough, fermenting and proofing it, dividing and moulding it, and baking it to profile.

groups.name: Dairy processing
groups.what: Making milk into product: separating and standardizing it, making cheese in the vat, and ripening and grading it.

groups.name: Grain milling
groups.what: Turning grain into flour, meal and feed: cleaning and tempering, roller milling and sifting, and pelleting.

groups.name: Brewing, winemaking and distilling
groups.what: Making beer, wine and spirits: mashing grain, crushing and pressing fruit, managing the fermentation, clarifying and filtering, distilling, aging in barrels and blending.

groups.name: Sterilization
groups.what: Killing organisms in product and on devices with heat or gas: pasteurizing, retorting, steam and ethylene oxide.

groups.name: Filling and packaging
groups.what: Filling and closing containers and running the packaging line and its in-line checks.

groups.name: Tablet manufacturing
groups.what: Making solid-dose drug product: weighing and dispensing, granulating and blending, compressing and coating tablets.

groups.name: Aseptic processing
groups.what: Making sterile product without contaminating it: qualified gowning, aseptic technique, filling and freeze drying.

skills.name: Sterile Filtration and Filter Integrity Testing

groups.name: Bioprocessing
groups.what: Making biologic drugs: media and buffers, growing cells, running the bioreactor, and purifying the product by filtration and chromatography.

groups.name: Laboratory analysis
groups.what: The quality control laboratory's chemical and microbiological tests on product, water and the manufacturing environment.

groups.name: Food product development
groups.what: Designing a food product and proving it: formulating to a target, judging it by panel, testing how long it keeps, and making the label true and legal.

groups.name: Chemical laboratory
groups.what: The chemistry laboratory's work: wet chemistry, spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, its records system, and proving its methods.

groups.name: Chemical processing
groups.what: Running a chemical plant: moving bulk liquids, reactors, distillation and the control room.

groups.name: Refinery units
groups.what: Running the continuous, high-temperature units of a refinery or petrochemical plant: fired heaters, process gas compressors and catalytic reactors.

groups.name: Pulp and paper making
groups.what: Making pulp, paper, board and tissue: cooking, washing and bleaching pulp, preparing stock, running the paper machine's wet and dry ends, creping and coating, and testing pulp and paper.

groups.name: Chemical recovery
groups.what: A kraft mill's recovery line: evaporating black liquor, firing the recovery boiler, recausticizing and reburning lime.

groups.name: Wood drying and panels
groups.what: Drying lumber in kilns, and making plywood, LVL, OSB, particleboard and MDF: peeling, drying, resin blending, forming and hot pressing.

groups.name: Kilns and grinding mills
groups.what: Firing and grinding minerals: rotary kilns for cement and lime, tunnel and periodic kilns for brick and ceramics, and the mills that grind raw meal, coal and cement.

groups.name: Fuels and cryogenics
groups.what: Proving fuel fit to use, and making and storing liquid oxygen and nitrogen.

groups.name: Nuclear plant operations
groups.what: Running a reactor plant and controlling its radiation and chemistry.

domains.name: Test
domains.what: Proving that a product works: electrical, functional, environmental, radio-frequency, vehicle and propulsion testing, and launch site operations.

groups.name: Electrical test
groups.what: Measuring and proving circuits with bench instruments: the multimeter and oscilloscope, continuity and high-voltage insulation tests.

groups.name: Functional test
groups.what: Running a product through its functional test, and writing the procedures and building the fixtures and programs that test it.

groups.name: Test systems
groups.what: The systems a test is run on: sensors and data acquisition, the program that runs the test, and simulation of what the unit will be connected to.

groups.name: Data bus testing
groups.what: Checking the data buses that link the electronic units of a vehicle or aircraft.

groups.name: RF test
groups.what: Measuring radio-frequency hardware: spectrum and network analyzers, electromagnetic compatibility and radar.

groups.name: Environmental testing
groups.what: Stressing a product with heat, vibration, vacuum and time to prove it survives and to learn how long it will last.

groups.name: Vehicle end-of-line testing
groups.what: The checks a finished vehicle passes before it leaves the plant: alignment, lamps, driver-assistance sensors, rolls, water, noises and final inspection.

groups.name: Propulsion testing
groups.what: Running motors and engines on a stand or dynamometer and reading the data they produce.

groups.name: Launch site operations
groups.what: Ground operations at a test stand or launch pad: cryogenic propellants, couplings and umbilicals, loading, and raising the vehicle.

domains.name: Maintenance
domains.what: Keeping machines, vehicles, ships and aircraft running: mechanical and electrical maintenance, power generation, fluid power, reliability methods, plant utilities, engines, vehicles and aircraft.

groups.name: Equipment maintenance
groups.what: Keeping production machines running: work orders, lubrication and scheduled upkeep, drives, conveyors, pumps and gearboxes, leveling and alignment, laser optics, and finding why a tool has stopped.

groups.name: Textile machine repair
groups.what: The fixer's work: setting, timing and repairing spinning machines, looms, knitting and tufting machines, and sewing machines.

groups.name: Electrical maintenance
groups.what: The plant electrician's work: reading the schematic, wiring and testing motors, running conduit, troubleshooting motor controls and working on 480 V power.

groups.name: Power generation and distribution
groups.what: Making electrical power and getting it to the load.

groups.name: Fluid power
groups.what: Hydraulics and pneumatics: reading the circuit, servicing and repairing components, then testing and troubleshooting the system.

groups.name: Reliability methods
groups.what: Maintaining by condition and by the numbers: thermography, oil and vibration analysis, and reliability metrics.

groups.name: Vacuum and utilities
groups.what: Running vacuum systems and finding their leaks, and the utilities a plant depends on: ultrapure water, compressed air, chillers and air handling.

groups.name: Plant utilities
groups.what: The steam, cooling and water a plant runs on.

groups.name: Engines and power plants
groups.what: Running and repairing the engines and plants that drive ships, vehicles and generators.

groups.name: Vehicles and heavy equipment
groups.what: Repairing wheeled and tracked vehicles and earthmoving equipment.

groups.name: Aircraft maintenance
groups.what: Servicing an aircraft's systems to its maintenance manual, running its engines and signing the work off.

groups.name: Aircraft systems
groups.what: Keeping an aircraft and its engines, fuel, electrical and air systems serviceable, on the line and in the shop.

skills.name: Helicopter Rotor and Drive System Maintenance

groups.name: Aircraft structural repair
groups.what: Repairing aircraft structure to the manufacturer's manual: corrosion treatment and sheet metal repair.

domains.name: Quality
domains.what: Measuring and assuring: measurement tools, inspection, coordinate metrology, calibration, statistics, corrective action and quality systems.

groups.name: Measurement tools
groups.what: The instruments an inspector or machinist measures a part with, from calipers, micrometers, indicators and pin gauges to gauge blocks, surface plate setups, profilometers and comparators.

groups.name: Part inspection
groups.what: Inspecting parts against the drawing: reading its geometric tolerances, checking in process, sampling a lot, the first article and the record.

groups.name: Lumber grading
groups.what: Grading lumber by eye and by scanner to the grading rules, and measuring its moisture.

groups.name: Coordinate metrology
groups.what: Measuring in three dimensions against the model: coordinate measuring machines, scanners and laser trackers.

groups.name: Calibration
groups.what: Checking measuring instruments against traceable standards, from hand gauges and meters to torque, pressure and temperature, and stating how far a measurement can be trusted.

groups.name: Statistical methods
groups.what: Using data to control and understand a process: control charts, capability, measurement system studies and designed experiments.

groups.name: Corrective action
groups.what: From the nonconforming part to the cause removed: reporting, disposition, root cause, 8D and corrective action.

groups.name: Quality planning and audit
groups.what: Planning quality into a process before it runs, and auditing the system that holds it: failure mode analysis, the control plan, the approval package and the quality system audit.

domains.name: Nondestructive testing
domains.what: Finding flaws without harming the part: visual, penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, radiographic and eddy current methods, and the inspection of composites.

groups.name: Visual methods
groups.what: Examining a surface by eye, directly or through a borescope.

groups.name: Penetrant methods
groups.what: Finding surface-breaking flaws with liquid penetrant: visible and fluorescent inspection and the checks that keep a line valid.

groups.name: Magnetic particle methods
groups.what: Finding surface and near-surface flaws in steel by magnetizing it: yoke and bench inspection, dry and wet fluorescent particles, and proving the field.

groups.name: Ultrasonic methods
groups.what: Inspecting with sound: thickness, calibration on reference blocks, straight and angle beam, immersion scanning, sizing flaws, phased array and time-of-flight diffraction.

groups.name: Radiographic methods
groups.what: Making a radiograph on film or a detector and reading it: exposure and image quality, film processing, digital and real-time systems, interpretation and computed tomography.

groups.name: Eddy current methods
groups.what: Finding cracks and measuring conductivity with induced currents: surface inspection, bolt holes, aircraft structure and arrays.

skills.name: Eddy Current Inspection of Aircraft Structure

groups.name: Composite inspection
groups.what: Finding disbonds, delaminations, porosity and impact damage in composite and bonded structure.

groups.name: NDT procedure development
groups.what: The Level III work behind an inspection: writing the procedure and designing the reference standard it is calibrated on.

domains.name: Safety
domains.what: Working without getting hurt: the habits, protective equipment and hazard controls every job on a floor starts from.

groups.name: Workplace safety
groups.what: The habits and protective equipment every person on a floor needs, and the training for work at height and in confined spaces.

groups.name: Hazardous energy
groups.what: Staying clear of the energy that injures: electricity, stored pressure, moving machines and robots, laser light and radiation.

groups.name: Hazardous materials
groups.what: Handling chemicals, dusts, process gases and explosives so nobody is exposed and nothing spills, burns or goes off.
